scripts.question: Tell me about a promising industry in your country. What makes it so successful and how do you see its future?
scripts.translation: 당신의 나라에서 유망한 산업 하나를 소개해 주세요. 무엇이 그 산업을 성공적으로 만들었고, 앞으로의 전망을 어떻게 보나요?
scripts.main_point: 한국의 대표 유망 산업은 반도체 → 삼성·SK하이닉스가 메모리 시장을 선도 → AI 확대로 반도체 중요성 증가 → 앞으로도 국가의 미래 산업으로 성장

key_expressions.tip: 산업의 중요성을 강하게 표현할 때 유용
반도체의 역할을 비유적으로 설명하는 기억하기 좋은 표현

key_expressions.expression: It’s not just a trend; it is the FUTURE of our country!

scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... If you ask me about the most promising industry in Korea, it is definitely THE SEMICONDUCTOR INDUSTRY. It is basically the backbone of our economy.

You know, companies like Samsung and SK Hynix are based in Korea. They are global giants and they literally lead the world's memory chip market. As a Korean, I feel SO PROUD of their success and their cutting-edge technology.

Actually, I am also an active investor in semiconductor stocks. So, I closely follow the news every single day. These days, with the rise of AI technology, semiconductors are becoming more important than ever. They are like the "BRAINS" of all modern devices.

So overall, Eva... I believe this industry will continue to grow rapidly. It’s not just a trend; it is the FUTURE of our country!

scripts.question: Who is your favorite singer or musical artist? What do you like about their music and performance?
scripts.translation: 가장 좋아하는 가수나 음악가는 누구인가요? 그 사람의 음악과 공연에서 어떤 점을 좋아하나요?
scripts.main_point: 가장 좋아하는 가수는 에일리 → 넓은 음역과 강력한 목소리 → 라이브와 퍼포먼스가 뛰어남 → 추천곡 ‘I Will Show You’ 소개

key_expressions.tip: 좋아하는 대상을 자신 있게 소개할 때 좋은 시작 표현
라이브 실력이나 퍼포먼스를 짧고 강하게 평가

scripts.script:
Without a doubt, Eva... My absolute favorite singer is AILEE. She is often called the "Korean Beyoncé," and she is an absolute powerhouse vocalist.

What I love most about her is her incredible vocal range. She can hit crazy high notes so effortlessly, and her voice is extremely rich and powerful. Every time she performs live on stage, she completely DOMINATES the crowd.

Also, her music has a very unique style. She blends emotional ballads with powerful pop songs. Even when she is doing intense choreography, her live vocals are FLAWLESS. It is just mind-blowing to watch.

So yeah, Eva... To me, she is not just a singer; she is a true diva. If you haven't heard her music yet, you should definitely check out her song "I Will Show You." It will literally give you goosebumps!

scripts.question: What is your favorite room in your house? Please describe it in detail and tell me what you usually do there.
scripts.translation: 집에서 가장 좋아하는 방은 어디인가요? 자세히 묘사하고 그곳에서 보통 무엇을 하는지 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 가장 좋아하는 곳은 침실 → 컴퓨터 게임으로 스트레스 해소 → 침대에서 유튜브·웹소설 즐김 → 편하게 쉬며 에너지를 충전하는 공간

key_expressions.tip: 휴식 공간을 묘사할 때 자연스러운 표현
퇴근 후 활동을 설명할 때 기억하기 좋은 표현

scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... I absolutely LOVE my bedroom the most. It is my favorite place because it is the perfect space for me to relax and UNWIND.

First of all, I have a nice computer in my room. So, after a long and stressful day at work, I often play online games with my friends. It really helps me DECOMPRESS and forget about work.

And also, my bed is the best! I love to just lie down on my bed and look at my smartphone. Usually, I watch funny videos on YouTube or read interesting web novels. To be honest, doing this after work is my favorite GUILTY PLEASURE. It is so relaxing.

So overall, Eva... this is what my favorite room looks like. My bedroom is like a HEAVEN to me because I can fully RECHARGE MY BATTERIES there. I just love being in my room!

scripts.question: How is the home you lived in as a child different from the one you live in now? What are the differences and similarities?
scripts.translation: 어릴 때 살던 집과 지금 사는 집은 어떻게 다른가요? 차이점과 공통점을 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 어릴 적 집은 평범한 브랜드 가구 중심 → 현재 집은 아내가 만든 DIY 가구 중심 → 개성과 따뜻함이 커짐 → 지금 집을 더 좋아함

key_expressions.tip: 비교 답변의 결론을 강하게 만드는 표현

scripts.script:
Eva, the biggest difference between my childhood home and my house now is definitely THE FURNITURE.

When I was a kid, my house was so simple. My mother bought normal furniture from big brands. Everything was just very PLAIN and HAD NO PERSONALITY. It looked exactly the same as other houses.

But now, my god! My house is full of DIY FURNITURE. Actually, my wife makes furniture as a hobby. She is incredibly HANDY, so she always makes tables and chairs for us in her free time. Thanks to her, our furniture STANDS OUT so much and makes our house completely ONE OF A KIND.

So yeah, Eva... Because of my wife's sweat and effort, our house feels so warm and unique. I love it much better than my childhood home!

scripts.question: Describe your living room. What kind of furniture or appliances do you have there, and which one is your favorite?
scripts.translation: 거실을 묘사해 주세요. 어떤 가구나 가전제품이 있고, 그중 가장 좋아하는 것은 무엇인가요?
scripts.main_point: 거실에서 가장 좋아하는 것은 안마의자 → 퇴근 후 바로 사용 → 피로를 풀어주는 작은 오아시스 같은 존재 → 하나만 고른다면 안마의자

key_expressions.tip: 퇴근 후 지친 모습을 생생하게 표현
피로나 스트레스가 풀리는 느낌을 자연스럽게 표현
바쁜 일상 속 휴식처를 비유적으로 표현

scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... My absolute favorite thing in my living room is my massage chair. It’s not just a machine, it’s like my PRIVATE MASSEUSE waiting for me.

Every day, after a stressful day at work, my body is completely broken. So, as soon as I get home, I THROW MYSELF into the chair. When I press start, it feels like a warm and big HUG.

Of course, there are other appliances like a big TV or an air conditioner, but they are just machines. ONLY this massage chair makes my fatigue MELT AWAY. It is like a small OASIS in my busy life.

So overall, Eva... If I can only keep ONE appliance in my living room, it will definitely be my massage chair. It completely RECHARGES MY BATTERIES every night!

scripts.question: Suppose that you have moved into a new building. Call the manager of the building and ask three or four questions about recycling.
scripts.translation: 새 건물로 이사했다고 가정해 보세요. 건물 관리자에게 전화해서 재활용에 대해 세네 가지 질문을 하세요.
scripts.main_point: 새 입주자라고 소개 → 재활용 장소 질문 → 배출 가능 시간 질문 → 종량제 봉투 구매 여부 질문 → 큰 박스 처리 장소 질문

key_expressions.expression: I have a few quick questions
Do you have a minute to talk?

scripts.script:
Hello, manager? Hi, this is the new tenant in unit 502. I just moved in yesterday, and I have a few quick questions about recycling. Do you have a minute to talk?

(상대 답변 듣고) Oh, great! Thanks.

First of all, where is the designated recycling area located? Is it in the basement, or outside near the main entrance?

(듣고) Ah, near the parking lot outside? Got it.

And also, are there specific days or times for throwing out the recyclables? Or can I just drop them off anytime?

(듣고) Oh, I can do it anytime 24/7? Wow, that's super convenient!

By the way, do I need to use official government bags for general waste, or does the building provide them?

(듣고) Ah, I have to buy them at the convenience store. Okay, no problem.

Lastly, what should I do with large cardboards from my moving boxes? Is there a separate place for those?

(듣고) Oh, right next to the recycling bins? Perfect!

Alright, that answers all my questions. Thank you so much for your help, manager! Have a great day!

scripts.question: A new resident from abroad has just moved in. However, he is throwing away garbage in the recycling bin. Other residents are very upset about that. Go to the new resident, explain the situation, and tell him about the recycling policy.
scripts.translation: 외국에서 온 새 입주자가 재활용통에 일반 쓰레기를 버리고 있습니다. 그 사람에게 상황과 재활용 규정을 설명하세요.
scripts.main_point: 새 이웃에게 인사 → 잘못된 쓰레기 배출을 부드럽게 알림 → 한국의 분리배출 규칙 설명 → 필요하면 도와주겠다고 제안

key_expressions.tip: 불편한 이야기를 부드럽게 꺼낼 때 유용
규칙을 간단히 정리해서 설명할 때 유용

key_expressions.expression: just knock on my door anytime

scripts.script:
Hi there! Excuse me... Are you the new resident in unit 503? Hi! I live next door in unit 502. Welcome to our building!

(듣고) Oh, nice to meet you, too!

Actually, I came over to give you a quick heads-up about something. I noticed earlier that you put general garbage into the recycling bin. To be honest, a few residents are a bit upset about it.

(듣고) Oh, no, no! Please don't worry! I totally get it. You just moved in from abroad, so you probably didn't know our building's policy, right?

(듣고) Yeah, I figured! Recycling in Korea can be a bit tricky.

So basically, we have to separate everything here. Food waste and general trash need to go into official plastic bags. You can easily buy them at the convenience store nearby. Only clean plastic, cans, and paper can go into the recycling bins.

(듣고) Ah, I see! You have those official bags already? That's great!

So yeah... If you ever need help sorting your trash, just knock on my door anytime. I'm happy to help!

(듣고) No problem at all! Have a great day!

scripts.question: You often host large parties and take out most of the recycling and garbage the next day. However, other residents in your building are not happy about it, and one of them has come to complain to you. Explain the situation and offer some suggestions to resolve the problem.
scripts.translation: 파티 후 많은 쓰레기와 재활용품을 한꺼번에 버려 다른 주민이 불만을 제기했습니다. 상황을 설명하고 해결 방안을 제안하세요.
scripts.main_point: 주민의 불만 확인 및 사과 → 집들이 때문에 쓰레기가 많았다고 설명 → 바로 재활용 구역 정리 제안 → 앞으로 나눠 버리거나 외부 폐기장 이용 약속

key_expressions.expression: I totally understand why you are frustrated.

key_expressions.tip: 상대가 해결책을 받아들였을 때 자연스러운 반응

key_expressions.expression: I promise it won't happen again.

scripts.script:
Oh, hi there! Are you the resident from unit 401? Wait, is something wrong? You look a bit upset.

(듣고) Oh... I am SO SO SORRY about that! I had no idea it was causing such a big problem for everyone.

To be honest, I hosted a small housewarming party last night, and we generated way more garbage and recycling than I expected. Since I didn't want to leave trash in my room, I threw it all out this morning at once. I am really sorry that it blocked the hallway and filled up the bins.

(듣고) Yeah, I totally understand why you are frustrated.

So, to fix this issue, I have a couple of suggestions.

First of all, I will go downstairs right now and clean up the recycling area. I'll stack the cardboards neatly and clear the way.

And second, from now on, when I have a party, I will take out the garbage in smaller batches throughout the day, or I will take it straight to the main waste center outside the building.

(듣고) Oh, that sounds good to you? That's a relief!

Again, I am really sorry for the inconvenience. I promise it won't happen again. Have a great day!

scripts.question: I'd like to know about how recycling is practiced in your country. What do people specifically do? Tell me how things are recycled.
scripts.translation: 당신의 나라에서는 재활용을 어떻게 하나요? 사람들이 구체적으로 무엇을 하는지 설명해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 한국은 엄격하게 분리수거 → 플라스틱·종이·음식물 등을 세분화하고 병을 씻어 라벨 제거 → 번거롭지만 환경을 위해 필요 → 제대로 하면 뿌듯함
scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... Korea has a very strict recycling system nationwide. We basically separate almost EVERYTHING, like plastic, paper, and food waste. For plastic bottles, people wash them out and peel off the vinyl labels before throwing them away.

To be frank, following all these strict rules can be pretty difficult and complicated. It takes a lot of time and effort to sort every single item properly.

However, in my opinion, I think it is definitely the right thing to do for the environment. Strict rules are necessary to cut down on waste and save our planet.

So personally, every time I finish sorting my trash properly, I feel a strong sense of accomplishment. Even though it’s not easy, I feel very PROUD that I am doing my part to protect the earth!

scripts.question: [Script]
scripts.translation: 어릴 때 재활용은 어땠나요? 재활용품을 가져가던 장소와 그곳에서 무엇을 했는지 자세히 설명해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 어릴 때는 지금보다 규칙이 덜 엄격 → 재활용품을 한꺼번에 큰 통에 넣음 → 아파트 입구 근처에서 주말마다 부모님을 도와 배출 → 지금이 환경에는 더 좋음

key_expressions.expression: NOT AS STRICT as it is now

scripts.script:
We didn't separate trash so carefully like today. Most recyclables—like plastic, paper, and cans—were just MIXED TOGETHER in big bins. We didn't even have to wash the bottles or take off the labels.

As for the recycling spot, there was a small place near my apartment entrance. It just had a few big plastic bins and nets on the ground. Every weekend, my job was to help my parents carry heavy bags down there.

So overall, Eva... recycling back then was much easier, but today’s system is much better for the earth!

## Question 3. [Memorable Episode] 분리수거 중 겪은 에피소드

Q. Problems sometimes occur while recycling. Tell me about something memorable related to recycling.

scripts.question: I was outside sorting my recyclables like plastics and paper, listening to music with my earbuds on. As I was putting things into different bins, one of my earbuds suddenly slipped right out of my ear and fell inside!
scripts.translation: 재활용을 하다가 문제가 생긴 적이 있나요? 재활용과 관련해 기억에 남는 일을 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 분리수거 중 무선 이어버드가 통 안으로 떨어짐 → 방에 돌아간 뒤 없어진 걸 깨닫고 당황 → 급히 내려가 통을 뒤져 찾음 → 이후 분리수거 전 이어버드를 뺌

key_expressions.expression: slipped right out of my ear

key_expressions.tip: 문제 해결 후 감정을 자연스럽게 표현

scripts.script:
Luckily, I searched through the bin and found it at the bottom! My hands got super dirty, but I was so relieved.

So overall, Eva... it was a very stressful day! Now, I always take off my earbuds before sorting my trash.

scripts.question: Discuss how people in your country get around every day. What forms of transportation do they use? Do they drive their own cars or use public transportation?
scripts.translation: 당신의 나라 사람들은 매일 어떻게 이동하나요? 자가용을 운전하나요, 대중교통을 이용하나요?
scripts.main_point: 한국은 지역에 따라 이동 방식이 다름 → 서울은 지하철·버스 중심 → 구미 같은 중소도시는 대중교통이 덜 편리 → 자가용 의존도가 높음

key_expressions.expression: it really depends on where you live
key_expressions.tip: 지역 차이를 설명하는 좋은 시작 문장
도시별 이동 수단 차이를 비교할 때 유용

scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... it really depends on where you live in Korea.

In big cities like Seoul, public transportation is extremely well-developed. Most people use the subway or buses for their daily commute because it is super fast and convenient.

However, in smaller cities like Gumi where I live, the situation is quite different. Public transportation is not as convenient, and we don't have a subway system. So, bus intervals can be quite long, which makes it a bit frustrating to get around without a car.

Because of this, most people in my city prefer driving their own cars for daily commuting and running errands.

So overall, Eva... while people in major cities heavily rely on subways and buses, residents in smaller cities like Gumi mostly depend on their personal cars!

scripts.question: Give a detailed description of the last time you used a form of transportation that was different than usual. Was this the first time you used this form of transportation? If so, did you enjoy the change? How long ago was this? Where were you going, and what did you do once you got there?
scripts.translation: 평소와 다른 교통수단을 최근 이용했던 경험을 자세히 말해 주세요. 어디에 갔고 무엇을 했나요?
scripts.main_point: 평소에는 자동차 여행 → 몇 달 전 아들과 KTX로 서울 주말여행 → 교통·주차 걱정 없이 편하게 이동 → 관광·음식·기념품 쇼핑 → 다시 이용하고 싶은 좋은 추억

key_expressions.expression: sit back, chat, and enjoy the scenery

scripts.script:
Oh, I actually have a great memory about this, Eva! A few months ago, I took the KTX bullet train with my son to visit Seoul for a weekend trip.

Usually, I always drive my own car when traveling, so taking the bullet train with my son was a very fresh experience. It wasn't my first time taking the KTX, but I really enjoyed the change because I didn't have to stress about traffic or parking! We could just sit back, chat, and enjoy the scenery together.

When we arrived in Seoul, we visited some famous places, had delicious food, and bought some cool souvenirs that my son really wanted. We had such a wonderful time together.

So overall, Eva... taking the bullet train was so much faster and more relaxing than driving! It was a super memorable trip with my son, and I’d definitely do it again.

scripts.question: What kinds of difficulties or problems have you faced related to transportation? What exactly was the problem? What did you do to resolve the problem? Tell this story in detail.
scripts.translation: 교통과 관련해 어떤 어려움이나 문제를 겪었나요? 문제와 해결 방법을 자세히 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 협력사 중요 미팅 가는 길 → 사고 때문에 고속도로가 거의 한 시간 정체 → 담당자에게 상황 설명 → 고속도로를 빠져나와 샛길 이용 → 미팅 시간에 맞춰 도착
scripts.script:
Oh, I have a very stressful story about this, Eva! Last year, I got stuck in a massive traffic jam on the highway on my way to an important meeting at a partner company.

I left my office early, and I was driving on the highway. Suddenly, traffic came to a complete standstill because of a major car accident ahead. I couldn't move at all for almost an hour, and I totally PANICKED!

To resolve the problem, I quickly took the nearest exit to get off the highway. I called the manager at the partner company to explain the situation, and then I used my navigation app to find a shortcut through local roads.

Luckily, the local roads were completely clear, so I was able to drive much faster. In the end, I arrived at the partner company just in time for the meeting!

So overall, Eva... it was a super nerve-wracking day! Now, I always check the traffic conditions before taking the highway.

scripts.question: What do you usually do to protect the environment in your daily life? Please describe some things you do regularly.
scripts.translation: 일상생활에서 환경을 보호하기 위해 보통 무엇을 하나요? 정기적으로 하는 활동을 설명해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 매일 작은 환경 보호 실천 → 플라스틱 병을 씻고 라벨 제거 → 포장이 적거나 재활용 소재 제품 구매 → 작은 습관도 도움이 된다고 생각

key_expressions.expression: I mean, it only takes a few seconds, right?
small habits can make a difference
key_expressions.meaning: 작은 습관도 변화를 만들 수 있다

scripts.script:
Well, to be honest, Eva... I try to do small things every day to help the environment.
You know, nothing too special, but I do my best.

First of all, I'm pretty serious about recycling.
For example, when I throw away plastic bottles, I always rinse them out with water first and remove the labels.
I mean, it only takes a few seconds, right?
So, I try not to be lazy about it.

Another thing I do is buy eco-friendly products.
When I go shopping, I try to choose products with less plastic packaging.
And if I have a choice, I usually go for products made from recycled materials.

Actually, I didn't really care about these things in the past.
But these days, I feel like small habits can make a difference.
You know what they say, every little bit helps!

So, yeah, Eva... recycling and buying eco-friendly products are just small things, but hey, it's better than doing nothing, right?

scripts.question: Tell me about a time when you realized an environmental problem was serious. What happened, and how did it affect you?
scripts.translation: 환경 문제가 심각하다고 깨달았던 때를 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고 어떤 영향을 받았나요?
scripts.main_point: 이번 여름 극심한 더위와 습도·갑작스러운 폭우 경험 → 밤새 에어컨을 켜야 할 정도 → 기후변화를 일상에서 직접 느낌 → 지구 보호의 시급성을 깨달음

key_expressions.expression: no longer just news on TV
key_expressions.meaning: 더 이상 TV 뉴스 속 이야기만이 아니다

key_expressions.expression: how urgently we need to protect our planet

scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... this summer has been just terrible because of the extreme heat! I was totally SHOCKED by how hot and humid it was in Korea.

The temperature was much higher than usual, and it rained heavily out of nowhere, just like a sudden squall. It felt like Korea's weather was turning into a tropical region. It was so hot and sticky during the day, and I had to keep the air conditioner on all night just to sleep.

Experiencing such extreme weather made me realize how serious global warming really is. It was no longer just news on TV. I could feel climate change right in my daily life.

So overall, Eva... this terrible summer was a huge wake-up call for me. It made me realize how urgently we need to protect our planet.

scripts.question: How has people’s attitude toward the environment changed compared to the past? What are some differences between the past and now?
scripts.translation: 과거와 비교해 환경에 대한 사람들의 태도는 어떻게 변했나요? 과거와 현재의 차이를 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 과거에는 환경 문제에 관심이 적고 일회용품을 많이 사용 → 현재는 텀블러·에코백 사용 증가 → 기업도 플라스틱 감축 노력 → 친환경 습관이 일상화
scripts.script:
To be honest, Eva... people’s attitude toward the environment has changed A LOT.

In the past, most people didn't care much about the environment. They used single-use plastics all the time, and recycling was not very strict back then.

However, nowadays, people care a lot more. Many people bring their own tumblers to coffee shops, and they use eco-bags at grocery stores. Also, companies are trying hard to reduce plastic waste.

So overall, Eva... people are much more conscious about protecting the earth now, and eco-friendly habits are a big part of our lives!

scripts.question: Tell me about the banks in your country. How do the banks look? Where are they located? What are their hours of operation? How often do you go to the bank?
scripts.translation: 당신의 나라 은행은 어떤 모습이고 어디에 있으며 영업시간은 어떤가요? 얼마나 자주 은행에 가나요?
scripts.main_point: 요즘은 오프라인 은행에 거의 가지 않음 → 모바일 뱅킹으로 잔액 확인·송금·공과금·계좌 관리 → 시간과 장소 제약이 없음 → 모바일 뱅킹이 우선 선택

key_expressions.expression: don't really go to physical banks very often
I can't even remember the last time
key_expressions.meaning: 마지막으로 언제 했는지 기억도 안 난다
key_expressions.tip: 거의 하지 않는 습관을 자연스럽게 강조

key_expressions.expression: why go to a bank when I can do everything on my phone?
key_expressions.meaning: 휴대폰으로 다 할 수 있는데 왜 은행에 가겠어요?

scripts.script:
Well, these days, most people in Korea don't really go to physical banks very often.

Instead, most people use mobile banking, and so do I.

You know, I do almost everything through mobile banking.

I can check my balance, transfer money, pay my bills, and even manage my accounts on my smartphone.

Actually, I can't even remember the last time I went to a bank in person.

Mobile banking is really convenient because I can use it anytime and anywhere.

I don't have to wait in line or worry about the bank's business hours.

I mean, why go to a bank when I can do everything on my phone?

So, mobile banking is definitely my first choice.

It's quick, easy, and saves me a lot of time.

scripts.question: What types of transactions usually take place at a bank? What kinds of responsibilities do the bank employees have? What things do clients request of the employees?
scripts.translation: 은행에서는 보통 어떤 거래가 이루어지고 은행 직원들은 어떤 일을 하나요? 고객들은 어떤 업무를 요청하나요?
scripts.main_point: 오프라인 은행은 거의 안 가서 직원 업무는 잘 모름 → 모바일 뱅킹으로 잔액·송금·공과금 처리 → 거래내역·신용카드 관리 → 빠르고 편해서 항상 모바일 뱅킹 이용

key_expressions.expression: I'm not really sure what bank employees do these days.
key_expressions.meaning: 요즘 은행 직원들이 정확히 무슨 일을 하는지 잘 모르겠어요

key_expressions.expression: with just a few taps on my phone

scripts.script:
Well, to be honest, I rarely go to a bank in person, so I'm not really sure what bank employees do these days.

You know, I do almost all of my banking through mobile banking.

There are so many things I can do with it.

For example, I can check my balance, transfer money, and pay my bills with just a few taps on my phone.

I can also check my transaction history and manage my credit cards.

Actually, I use mobile banking almost every day.

The best thing is that I don't have to visit a bank or wait in line.

I can take care of everything anytime and anywhere.

I mean, everything I need is right there on my phone.

So, these days, whenever I need to do something related to banking, mobile banking is always my first choice.

It's simple, fast, and super convenient.

scripts.question: Have you ever experienced that you needed to find help to solve a problem? For example, has your credit card ever malfunctioned or have you ever lost your credit card? Tell me about a circumstance involving a bank account or credit card as vividly as possible.
scripts.translation: 은행 계좌나 신용카드 문제를 해결하기 위해 도움을 받아야 했던 경험을 가능한 생생하게 말해 주세요.
scripts.main_point: 아들에게 신용카드를 줌 → 준 사실을 잊고 결제 알림을 받아 도난으로 착각 → 고객센터에 전화 → 집 근처 편의점 결제라는 말을 듣고 기억남 → 안도하고 사과

key_expressions.expression: at least my card wasn't stolen

scripts.script:
Oh, actually, I have a funny story about my credit card.

A few months ago, I gave my credit card to my son because he wanted to buy something at a convenience store near my house.

But I totally forgot about it.

A little later, I suddenly got a notification on my phone saying that my credit card had been used.

I was really surprised and started to panic.

I thought, "Oh my gosh! Someone is using my credit card!"

So, I immediately called the bank's customer service center and explained what had happened.

The employee checked the transaction and told me that my card had been used at a convenience store near my house.

And then, it suddenly hit me.

I remembered that I had given my credit card to my son!

I felt so relieved, but at the same time, I was really embarrassed.

I quickly said, "Oh, I'm so sorry. I completely forgot that I gave my card to my son."

Luckily, the employee was very understanding, so I apologized again and ended the call.

Well, it was a little embarrassing, but at least my card wasn't stolen!
